decision: capsule replaces the placeholder-substitution runbook with a single interactive host-side wizard.sh that scaffolds a new sandboxed DevPod+Podman+VSCodium repo pre-wired for autonomous agent work (tagdexer + decision log + taskboard + 9 generic hooks).
intent: Make standing up a new agent-ready repo a one-command, hiccup-free process whose output never clashes with existing repos/containers.
context: Prior flow was a README with <TOKEN> placeholders substituted by hand — error-prone (manual port picking, name sanitization, memory-bridge keys). The wizard derives all of that deterministically and verifies isolation before declaring success.

decision: The wizard NEVER emits --pid=host in a container's runArgs. That flag was the root cause of pickles' VSCodium remote window failing to attach.
intent: Prevent the single hardest-to-diagnose failure mode from ever recurring in a generated repo.
context: --pid=host gives the container the host's process table. open-remote-ssh checks 'is a server already running?' by scanning processes; it then saw ANOTHER container's codium-server (same VSCodium build hash), falsely concluded a server was up, took the reuse path, found no connection-token file, and aborted with exitCode 1. A plain ssh shell worked fine because it doesn't inspect processes — only the VSCodium client does. Removing --pid=host and recreating fixed it.
consequence: GPU repos get only --device=nvidia.com/gpu=all + --security-opt=label=disable. If a repo genuinely needs host-process visibility, that must be solved another way, never via --pid=host on a VSCodium-attached container.

decision: The wizard's GPU path auto-pins the CDI spec to a version this Podman can parse instead of hardcoding 0.5.0; it probes, regenerates only if unresolvable, and verifies end-to-end.
intent: Survive driver/toolkit updates that silently break GPU passthrough.
context: A driver update (595.58.03->595.71.05) left /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml at CDI spec 0.7.0. Podman 4.9.3 parses only <=0.6.0, so every device read as 'unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all' and the container could not start. nvidia-ctk >=1.17 dropped the --cdi-version flag and auto-emits the minimum-required (often 0.7.0+); the working fix was downgrading the toolkit to 1.16.2 (emits 0.5.0) and regenerating. The wizard: pin to 0.6.0 if the flag exists, else regenerate and verify; on failure it tells the owner to downgrade the toolkit.
consequence: GPU verification is end-to-end (podman run ... nvidia-smi -L) so a silent CPU fallback can't pass as success.

decision: tagdexer is deployed by copying its CLI files into the new repo, but .tagdexerrc genericPath points at the IN-CONTAINER mount /workspaces/tagdexer-source, not the host /mnt/d/repos/tagdexer.
intent: Avoid silent degradation of the decision-log/index tooling inside the sandbox.
context: The deployed tagdexer CLI reads the central source at runtime for the shared alias vocabulary and trackdexer config. If genericPath resolves to a host path that doesn't exist in the container, the CLI still runs but silently drops the shared layer (tags show [project] instead of [shared+project]). The container bind-mounts central tagdexer at /workspaces/tagdexer-source; pointing genericPath there keeps the shared layer active. Verified in fbad: 449 shared tags resolve. decisions.jsonl is JSONL and is left absent on a fresh repo (absent == empty; pre-creating [] is invalid).

decision: taskboard is deployed self-contained and wired via its own install.sh --reset (empties lists+domains, jq-merges its 2 hooks); the wizard installs the 9 .claude hooks itself and delegates the 2 taskboard hooks to that installer.
intent: Reuse each subsystem's own deploy seam rather than reinventing hook-wiring, and guarantee a pristine board with no foreign pending work.
context: taskboard has no genericPath/central dependency (unlike tagdexer) — it is a standalone Node CLI. Its install.sh is idempotent, backs up settings.json, and merges SessionStart-awareness + PostToolUse-nudge hooks. The block_pip_install.sh and block_git_writes.sh hooks are deliberately excluded from the generic set (owner instruction).

decision: Dockerfile heredoc built the extra-apt line via $() command substitution, which strips the trailing newline and glues the continuation backslash onto the && rm line; apt then parses an empty package name and the image build fails with 'Unable to locate package'.
intent: Record why EXTRA_APT now expands inline on its own continuation line so the substitution pattern is never reintroduced.
context: First real run with non-empty extra apt (receipt_digitizer, libgl1 libglib2.0-0) failed at image build; all prior repos used empty extra apt, where the $() branch emits nothing and the bug is invisible. Fixed by replacing EXTRA_APT_LINE/$() with a literal EXTRA_APT continuation line inside the heredoc; empty case yields a harmless blank continuation. NOTE: central tracker.js run from another repo writes the log next to itself, not in cwd — this repo needs a local tracker.js deploy for logging.

decision: The isolation verify used pgrep -af synochat over ssh, which always reports HOST-VISIBLE because the remote shell own command line contains the string synochat; switched to pgrep -x.
intent: Stop the wizard from emitting a false could-not-confirm-isolation warning on every build of a correctly isolated container.
context: receipt_digitizer build verified manually: container sees 19 processes with PID 1 = sh and pgrep -x synochat empty while the host runs 9 synochat processes, so isolation was real and the HOST-VISIBLE result was the check matching itself. pgrep -f scans full cmdlines and excludes only its own pid, not the bash -c parent that carries the pattern string.

decision: The wizard now supports existing repos: it backs up a prior .claude/settings.json to settings.json.pre-wizard, carries taskboard lists/ and domains.json across the refresh, offers to move a host-built .venv to .venv_host_backup (post-create also rebuilds any venv whose python does not execute in-container), and the /workspaces symlink step checks readlink first, only sudos for missing links, and warns with manual commands instead of dying when sudo is unavailable.
intent: Make containerising an established repo as safe as scaffolding an empty one, with no silent loss of hooks, pending work, or environments.
context: First existing-repo run (receipt_digitizer) surfaced the gaps: settings.json would have been clobbered had one existed, taskboard rm -rf would drop pending lists, the stale host venv had to be hand-renamed, and the unconditional sudo killed the script under a non-interactive agent run. Verified end-to-end on a scratch repo seeded with all four conditions; all preserved branches and the sudo-warn path fired.

decision: The wizard now writes a Container/Host Execution Boundary appendix into every repo CLAUDE.md with that repo real paths substituted; fresh stubs include it, existing CLAUDE.md files get it appended once keyed on the heading, never duplicated.
intent: Ensure every container agent permanently knows the bind-mount semantics and the protocol for host-side operations it cannot perform itself.
context: Owner drafted and finalized the appendix in receipt_digitizer after an agent confusion about host vs container command execution; path-substitution wording was relaxed to symlink-first because the wizard creates /workspaces/<name> on the host. Verified on scratch repos: fresh stub, append-to-existing, and double-run idempotency all correct.

decision: wizard.sh gained a GUI mode, auto-enabled when a display plus kdialog or zenity is present: repo selection becomes a native folder-picker dialog rooted at /mnt/d/repos, remaining questions become input/yesno dialogs, derived values confirm via a summary dialog, and die() mirrors errors to a GUI error box; --no-gui restores terminal prompts.
intent: Let the owner set up a repo by browsing and clicking the folder instead of typing names into a terminal.
context: kdialog (KDE-native, Dolphin-style picker) is preferred but not currently installed; zenity is the working fallback and the code auto-upgrades to kdialog if installed later. Picker result is validated to be directly under /mnt/d/repos. Verified headlessly with a stubbed kdialog: full GUI-path scaffold run, nested-folder rejection, and --no-gui terminal regression all pass. Progress output still prints to the terminal (wizard-launch.sh keeps Terminal=true for sudo + logs).

decision: payload/memory gained feedback_no_askuserquestion.md so every wizard-scaffolded repo seeds the no-AskUserQuestion rule alongside the no-co-author rule.
intent: Make agents in all new containers ask questions inline in chat instead of via the structured AskUserQuestion UI.
context: Owner instruction; receipt_digitizer already carries the memory manually. Wizard step 6b copies payload memories into the host project memory dir without clobbering and merges MEMORY.md index lines without duplicating, so existing repos pick it up on any re-run.

decision: Made the wizard portable + added a single-file self-extracting USB installer (make-usb-installer.sh -> capsule-install.sh). wizard.sh now derives REPOS_ROOT, CENTRAL_TAGDEXER, CENTRAL_SETSQUARE, HOST_CLAUDE_PROJECTS and the credentials mount from its own location and $HOME (all env-overridable); no hardcoded /mnt/d or /home/desktop paths remain. The installer packs capsule+tagdexer+setsquare as a base64 tgz after a __CAPSULE_PAYLOAD__ marker.
intent: wizard.sh only worked where the three sibling repos already existed at a hardcoded /mnt/d/repos; a fresh machine had none of them. Enables: drop one 6M file on a USB, run from anywhere, extract, then wizard.sh just works.
context: Excludes .git and node_modules (~194M build-time deps not needed at runtime since the shipped *.vsix are prebuilt and copied CLI files are plain node scripts). Installer defaults to $HOME/repos, -d picks a root, -y chains into wizard, and it guards against clobbering an existing install. Round-trip verified: extraction, both vsix present, no node_modules/.git leak, extracted wizard.sh syntax OK.

decision: Decoupled the target repo location from REPOS_ROOT. Repo to containerise can now live ANYWHERE: set via $REPO_PATH, GUI browse, or absolute-path/bare-name prompt. Removed the 'must be directly under REPOS_ROOT' die. HOST_PROJECT_KEY now derives from the real absolute path (tr '_/' '--') instead of a hardcoded -mnt-d-repos- prefix. Rebuilt capsule-install.sh.
intent: Portability demands the repo location AND the wizard/sources install dir both be configurable; the old hard constraint forced every target repo to sit under REPOS_ROOT and produced a wrong claude project key off /mnt/d.
context: REPOS_ROOT still governs where the wizard+sources install and sibling mounts resolve; only the target repo is now independent of it. Verified: syntax OK, embedded wizard carries the new logic, key derivation correct for arbitrary paths.

decision: DevPod's podman support is NOT a downloadable provider — 'devpod provider add podman' 404s (loft-sh/devpod-provider-podman has no latest provider.yaml). The working setup uses the built-in internal 'docker' provider renamed to podman with DOCKER_PATH pointed at the podman binary: 'devpod provider add docker --name podman -o DOCKER_PATH=/usr/bin/podman && devpod provider use podman'. Confirmed from source machine workspace.json (DOCKER_PATH value=/usr/bin/podman, userProvided) and reproduced on a fresh Debian 13 host.
intent: wizard.sh calls 'devpod up' but never adds/configures a provider; a fresh devpod install has none, so the build fails at the last step. This is the missing prerequisite that blocked the first real portable run on Debian 13.
context: Surfaced deploying to Debian 13 (trixie), devpod v0.6.15, podman 5.4.2. Should be folded into wizard preflight (auto-add the provider if absent) and/or the README runbook. Provider is host-global, not per-repo, so it's a one-time host setup.

decision: Wizard gained AMD device-passthrough options: NPU (XDNA, /dev/accel/accel0) and iGPU (ROCm, /dev/dri + /dev/kfd + video/render groups), each with host preflight and post-build verify, mirroring the GPU path. All passed devices share --security-opt=label=disable for SELinux.
intent: This Fedora/Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350 host replaces the old NVIDIA box; agent workloads (PaddleOCR/LiLT experiments) need accelerator access. Passthrough is the wizard's job; the in-container runtime stack is not.
context: Probed host: amdxdna + /dev/accel present; /dev/dri + /dev/kfd present; container vscode uid 1000 == host uid so nodes are openable. Verified runArgs JSON for all GPU/NPU/iGPU combos.
consequence: Passthrough != acceleration: NPU needs XRT+Vitis-AI EP; iGPU needs a ROCm-matched torch wheel (gfx1152 => ROCm 7.13+). Wizard warns, does not install these.

decision: Wizard ingests a per-repo 'repo-needs' JSON (apt/pip/build_steps/volumes/env/verify) produced by an agent run IN the target repo via a paste-to-agent prompt; it routes each field to the right file (apt->Dockerfile, pip/build_steps/verify->post-create.sh, volumes->named mounts, env->containerEnv). Model prewarm + verify are NON-FATAL.
intent: System libs vs venv deps can't be fully auto-detected; delegating analysis to the in-repo agent is reliable. Non-fatal prewarm stops an app-level model/version crash (e.g. paddle 3.0.0 vs PP-OCRv6) from leaving the user with no container.
context: Built after receipt_digitizer OCR builds aborted the whole container on a create_pipeline() crash. Verified generated post-create.sh + devcontainer.json are valid for the real JSON.
consequence: Wizard cannot safely auto-edit requirements.txt; surfaces the agent's notes as warnings instead. Named volumes over existing bind paths re-populate once (empty on first mount).

decision: Wizard auto-generates .grok/hooks/agent-hooks.json by transforming the finalized .claude/settings.json hooks block (prefix ../../, widen PreToolUse matcher), so a Grok agent fires the SAME 11 hooks as Claude with no duplicate scripts.
intent: Grok agents must onboard identically to Claude out of the box. Reusing the existing hook scripts (not copying into a vendor-neutral dir) avoids drift and stays auto-synced with settings.json.
context: Grok resolves hook paths relative to its config dir, not repo root (observed ../../agent-hooks/ in a hand-made config). Transform verified to emit 11 hooks, valid JSON.

decision: Moved the wizard's per-host assumptions (container timezone, scaffold git identity) out of the script into a first-run machine profile saved under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/capsule/machine.conf and reused on every later run
intent: Make the wizard portable enough to publish, capturing a new user's host values once instead of hand-editing them into the source
context: wizard.sh hard-coded TZ=UTC into every generated devcontainer.json and stamped git-init commits as owner/owner@local; both are host/owner-specific and blocked sharing the repo publicly
constraints: Profile file is sourced under set -euo pipefail, so keys are pre-initialised and written with printf %q; a newly added key re-prompts for only that key
consequence: machine.conf is now the single place to change per-host values; the repo's own git history was also rewritten to one canonical author/committer identity (Oisin McGrath), which changed all commit hashes — the nas remote still holds the old history until a force-push

decision: Made tagdexer deployment optional via a first-run TAGDEXER_MODE policy (always/never/ask) and defaulted its source to the copy vendored in this repo, with the tagdexer and setsquare mounts/symlinks/settings/CLAUDE.md all conditional
intent: Let the wizard install and run standalone from GitHub with no external sibling repos, and let a user opt out of tagdexer
context: wizard.sh required sibling tagdexer/ and setsquare/ checkouts (preflight died without tagdexer; devcontainer.json always mounted both), blocking portable install and forcing tagdexer on every repo
constraints: Mount/settings lines use the leading-comma style so an empty sister set collapses to valid JSON (verified across always/ask/never x setsquare-present/absent)
consequence: Standalone clones self-contain tagdexer via WIZ_DIR/tagdexer; setsquare is skipped when absent; never-mode repos get a taskboard-only CLAUDE.md and no .tagdexerrc

decision: Extended the first-run machine profile to record tagdexer/setsquare source paths — asking for an existing checkout, or offering to git clone tagdexer from github.com/oisinmcgrath/tagdexer into ~/projects, saved as MACHINE_TAGDEXER_PATH/MACHINE_SETSQUARE_PATH
intent: Let a fresh host acquire the shared tools during setup instead of failing when the sibling repos are absent
context: Self-containment gave a vendored tagdexer fallback but no way to point at or fetch the real shared source; setsquare had no acquisition path at all
constraints: Resolution priority: explicit $CENTRAL_* env > saved profile path > sibling checkout > vendored copy; a missing NON-env saved path falls back to vendored, a missing env path is kept so the typo surfaces at deploy-time die
consequence: machine.conf gains MACHINE_TAGDEXER_PATH/MACHINE_SETSQUARE_PATH; setsquare '-' sentinel means none; clone is opt-in and network-guarded with a vendored fallback
